title: Getting going
explanation_md:
Welcome! In this tutorial you write Python in the box and press **Run**. Python runs in your browser, so the first load takes a few seconds.

Try this line:

```python
print("hello")
```

`print` shows whatever is inside the brackets. The quote marks tell Python that `hello` is text. The output appears underneath the box. Run again and the old output is replaced.

**Mistakes are normal.** When something is wrong, Python stops and shows an error. Read the **last line** of the error first: it names the problem, such as `SyntaxError` or `NameError`. The message also gives a **line number**. The mistake is on that line, or just before it.

Common slips:

- a missing bracket: `print("hello"`
- a missing quote mark: `print("hello)`
- a misspelt name: `pritn("hello")`

Fix the one character that is wrong. There is no need to retype everything.

A `#` starts a **comment**. Python ignores the rest of that line, so comments are notes for people:

```python
# This line is a note
print("hello")  # so is this part
```

Each task below is checked for you. You get a hint after one try and a worked solution after two. **New example** gives you fresh text to practise with, as often as you like.

templates.title: Fix the broken line
templates.prompt_md:
This code should print two lines:

```
Welcome to the café
Table @@table@@ is ready
```

One line is broken. Fix it so the code prints exactly that.
templates.starter_code:
print("Welcome to the café")
print("Table @@table@@ is ready"
templates.reference:
print("Welcome to the café")
print("Table @@table@@ is ready")
hints: The second line is missing its closing bracket `)` at the end.
wrong_examples:
print("Welcome to the café")
print("Table is ready")
print("Table @@table@@ is ready")
templates.solution_md: Add `)` at the end of the second line, so every `(` has a matching `)`.

templates.title: Say hello
templates.prompt_md: Type `print("hello")` in the box and press **Run** (or Ctrl+Enter; ⌘+Enter on a Mac). You should see `hello` underneath.
templates.starter_code: # Type your code below this line
hints: Type exactly: `print("hello")`, with the brackets and the quote marks.

templates.title: Change the message
templates.prompt_md:
Change the text inside the quote marks so the code prints:

```
Hello from the café
```

Run it again; the new output replaces the old.
hints: Only change the words between the quote marks. Keep the brackets and quotes.

templates.title: Break it, then fix it
templates.prompt_md: This line has a mistake: the closing bracket is missing. Press **Run** first and read the **last line** of the error. Then fix it so it prints `hello`.
hints: Every `(` needs a matching `)`. Add one at the end of the line.

templates.title: Change the text
templates.prompt_md:
Change this code so it prints exactly:

```
@@msg@@
```
templates.generator:
def generate(rng):
    return {'msg': rng.choice(['Latte please', 'One flat white', 'Tea for two', 'Cake of the day', 'Open at 8am', 'Closed on Sundays', 'Free refills today', 'Two scones, please', 'Hot chocolate time', 'Table for four', 'Oat milk available', 'Last orders at 5pm'])}
hints: Replace `Good morning` with the new text, keeping the quote marks: `print("@@msg@@")`.

templates.title: Print two lines
templates.prompt_md:
Add a second `print` so the code prints these two lines:

```
@@line1@@
@@line2@@
```
templates.starter_code:
print(@@line1@@)
# add a second line here
hints: Each `print` makes its own line. Add `print("@@line2@@")` on a new line underneath.

templates.title: Fix a missing bracket
templates.prompt_md:
This code should print:

```
Table @@table@@ is ready
Enjoy your @@drink@@
```

Run it, read the last line of the error, and fix the broken line.
hints: The error points at line 1 or just after it. The first line needs a `)` at the end.
wrong_examples:
print("Table @@table@@ is ready"))
print(@@enjoy@@)
print("Table @@table@@ is ready")

templates.title: Fix a missing quote mark
templates.prompt_md:
This code should print:

```
Table @@table@@ wants @@cups@@ cups of tea
```

One quote mark is missing. Find it and fix it.
hints: Text needs a quote mark at **both** ends. Add `"` just before the closing bracket.
wrong_examples:
print("Table @@table@@ wants @@cups@@ cups of tea)")
print("Table @@table@@ wants @@cups@@ cups")

templates.title: Fix a misspelt name
templates.prompt_md:
This code should print:

```
Order @@order@@ is ready
Thank you!
```

Run it, read the last line of the error (it names the problem), and fix it.
hints: `NameError` means Python doesn't know a name. Look at the spelling of `print` on line 1.
wrong_examples:
Print("Order @@order@@ is ready")
print("Thank you!")
print("Order @@order@@ is ready")
